interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

crop_categories: Tree and vine crops (olive, almond, grape, citrus)
residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)

assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)

post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 14.9 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3829.0-5625.0 m3/ha/yr (central 4660.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.0 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 4.9 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.08 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction

interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.0 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed

Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.87 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

scenarios.name: Bench terraces with soil conservation and drip irrigation (sloping land)
crop_categories: Tree and vine crops (olive, almond, grape, citrus)
residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
residual root-zone salinity above 4 dS/m limits sensitive crops
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)
SoilGrids vs WoSIS arid RMSE; low skill in deserts
assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)
expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)
relative erosion index (RUSLE-type structure)
FAO suitability class boundaries on relative yield (S1>=0.8, S2 0.6-0.8, S3 0.4-0.6 [assumed], N<0.4)
simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

data_sources: WoSIS 2023-12 snapshot (ISRIC; CC BY / public-domain subset) - ECe training labels
Hassani et al. 2020 (Mendeley Data, CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP training points
SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC, CC BY 4.0) - pH, SOC, texture, CF, BD, CEC
SoilGrids 2017 BDRICM (ISRIC) - depth to bedrock
WorldClim 2.1 bioclim + elevation (CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP covariates
TerraClimate 2011-2020 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) - rainfall, ET0
Copernicus GLO-30 DEM - slope
geoBoundaries gbOpen JOR ADM1 (CC BY 2.5) - boundary

limiting_factors.detail: annual rainfall 145.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 120.0 mm) vs barley season ET 594.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 18.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply
mean slope 12.4 deg (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, 50 m slope aggregated to 250 m)
relative water-erosion index 0.28 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)
coarse fragments about 30.0 vol %

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 12.4 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 4949.0-6977.0 m3/ha/yr (central 5946.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.1 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 4.1 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 4046.0-5801.0 m3/ha/yr (central 4871.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.2 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: 1.0 t/ha gypsum (0.3 m, effectiveness 0.5-0.9 assumed) lowers ESP 5.1 -> 5.0 %
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.57 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.expected_effect: slope 8.7 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3836.0-5596.0 m3/ha/yr (central 4668.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.0 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 3.6 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.79 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.9 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 3.7 % <= 5 % target)

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.71 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)

interventions.expected_effect: slope 9.7 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3308.0-4832.0 m3/ha/yr (central 4152.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.8 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 2.0 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.98 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

crop_categories: Tree and vine crops (olive, almond, grape, citrus)

secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
residual root-zone salinity above 4 dS/m limits sensitive crops

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)

assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)
expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)
relative erosion index (RUSLE-type structure)

simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 11.2 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 3594.0-5391.0 m3/ha/yr (central 4445.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.8 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed

interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.12 %; improves water holding and infiltration

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: reduce ECe 7.4 -> 4.1 dS/m (simulated); reclamation leaching depth 0.07 m water per m soil = 406.0 m3/ha one-off (C/C0 = exp(-k r), k 1.6-2.3, FAO IDP29 80-90% removal at r=1)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: 2.2 t/ha gypsum (0.3 m, effectiveness 0.5-0.9 assumed) lowers ESP 10.5 -> 5.0 %
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.97 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.6 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: 1.5 t/ha gypsum (0.3 m, effectiveness 0.5-0.9 assumed) lowers ESP 5.3 -> 5.0 %
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.57 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)

limiting_factors.detail: annual rainfall 48.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 39.0 mm) vs barley season ET 683.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 5.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 6668.0-10001.0 m3/ha/yr (central 7721.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: reduce ECe 7.2 -> 4.1 dS/m (simulated); reclamation leaching depth 0.12 m water per m soil = 749.0 m3/ha one-off (C/C0 = exp(-k r), k 1.6-2.3, FAO IDP29 80-90% removal at r=1)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: 5.8 t/ha gypsum (0.3 m, effectiveness 0.5-0.9 assumed) lowers ESP 10.4 -> 5.0 %
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.9 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Salt/sodicity-tolerant crop selection (date palm, barley, tall wheatgrass, olive)
interventions.description: Choose crops whose Maas-Hoffman threshold exceeds the achievable root-zone ECe (FAO Table 4) and whose ESP class tolerates the residual sodicity.
interventions.expected_effect: crop choice keeps relative yield >= 0.6 at ECe 7.3 dS/m (post-reclamation, simulated)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: reduce ECe 8.0 -> 4.0 dS/m (simulated); reclamation leaching depth 0.2 m water per m soil = 1176.0 m3/ha one-off (C/C0 = exp(-k r), k 1.6-2.3, FAO IDP29 80-90% removal at r=1)

interventions.expected_effect: slope 10.2 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 4153.0-6153.0 m3/ha/yr (central 5062.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.1 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: 0.8 t/ha gypsum (0.3 m, effectiveness 0.5-0.9 assumed) lowers ESP 5.6 -> 5.0 %
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.76 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)

interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.78 %; improves water holding and infiltration

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.

interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

crop_categories: Tree and vine crops (olive, almond, grape, citrus)
residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)

assumed; no local validation

climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)

pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)

limiting_factors.detail: annual rainfall 247.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 219.0 mm) vs barley season ET 559.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 35.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Bench terraces with stone/earth risers and runoff diversion
interventions.description: Converts slopes up to a practical limit (assumed 20-30 deg, soil depth >= 40 cm) into cultivable benches and reduces water erosion; abandonment/poor maintenance is the main failure mode.
interventions.expected_effect: slope 9.5 deg made cultivable (limit 20-30 deg, depth >= 40 cm); erosion reduced (assumed 50-90 %)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 4006.0-5914.0 m3/ha/yr (central 4881.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 0.9 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: 0.5 t/ha gypsum (0.3 m, effectiveness 0.5-0.9 assumed) lowers ESP 5.0 -> 5.0 %
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.64 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 0.0-0.0 m3/ha/yr (central 0.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.0 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 3.1 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.87 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

scenarios.name: Drip irrigation with fresh groundwater + reclamation leaching, gypsum and organic amendment
residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)
SoilGrids vs WoSIS arid RMSE; low skill in deserts
assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)
expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)
relative erosion index (RUSLE-type structure)
FAO suitability class boundaries on relative yield (S1>=0.8, S2 0.6-0.8, S3 0.4-0.6 [assumed], N<0.4)
simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

data_sources: WoSIS 2023-12 snapshot (ISRIC; CC BY / public-domain subset) - ECe training labels
Hassani et al. 2020 (Mendeley Data, CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP training points
SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC, CC BY 4.0) - pH, SOC, texture, CF, BD, CEC
SoilGrids 2017 BDRICM (ISRIC) - depth to bedrock
WorldClim 2.1 bioclim + elevation (CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP covariates
TerraClimate 2011-2020 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018) - rainfall, ET0
Copernicus GLO-30 DEM - slope
geoBoundaries gbOpen JOR ADM1 (CC BY 2.5) - boundary

limiting_factors.detail: Model 1 class 5: legal/environmental restriction. Restoration potential is not assessed; the restriction itself is the limiting factor.

annual rainfall 291.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 245.0 mm) vs barley season ET 530.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 41.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range. interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.99 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)

interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 0.0-0.0 m3/ha/yr (central 0.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 2.0 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 5.7 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.52 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

scenarios.name: Drip irrigation with fresh groundwater + reclamation leaching, gypsum and organic amendment
residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)
SoilGrids vs WoSIS arid RMSE; low skill in deserts
assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)
expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)
relative erosion index (RUSLE-type structure)
FAO suitability class boundaries on relative yield (S1>=0.8, S2 0.6-0.8, S3 0.4-0.6 [assumed], N<0.4)
simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

data_sources: WoSIS 2023-12 snapshot (ISRIC; CC BY / public-domain subset) - ECe training labels
Hassani et al. 2020 (Mendeley Data, CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP training points
SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC, CC BY 4.0) - pH, SOC, texture, CF, BD, CEC
SoilGrids 2017 BDRICM (ISRIC) - depth to bedrock
WorldClim 2.1 bioclim + elevation (CC BY 4.0) - ECe/ESP covariates

limiting_factors.detail: Model 1 class 5: legal/environmental restriction. Restoration potential is not assessed; the restriction itself is the limiting factor.

annual rainfall 327.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 280.0 mm) vs barley season ET 525.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 48.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply
relative water-erosion index 0.17 (RUSLE-type structure, not a soil-loss prediction; wind/flash-flood erosion not modelled)

limiting_factors.detail: Model 1 class 5: legal/environmental restriction. Restoration potential is not assessed; the restriction itself is the limiting factor.

annual rainfall 292.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 261.0 mm) vs barley season ET 548.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 42.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 0.0-0.0 m3/ha/yr (central 0.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: initial ECe 1.3 dS/m is already low; only maintenance leaching fraction needed
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 4.2 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 0.76 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]

interventions.name: Subsurface/open drainage and leachate disposal (evaporation pond)
interventions.description: Leaching only works if leachate can leave the root zone; saline basins with shallow saline water tables are effectively non-reclaimable. No water-table data are available here, so drainage feasibility is probabilistic (decreasing with initial ECe).
interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.expected_effect: enables leachate removal; feasibility decreases with initial ECe (probabilistic, no water-table data)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

scenarios.name: Drip irrigation with fresh groundwater + reclamation leaching, gypsum and organic amendment
residual_risks: groundwater depletion: fossil/non-renewable aquifer abstraction (aquifer yield and licence not assessed)
secondary salinisation/sodification if leaching or drainage fails
wind erosion/dust and flash-flood erosion are not modelled
soil depth and SOC come from third-party maps with no local validation (SoilGrids deserts: low skill for SOC)

uncertainty.basis: SoilGrids 2.0 vs WoSIS measured, arid held-out sites (RMSE)
SoilGrids vs WoSIS arid RMSE; low skill in deserts
assumed; no local validation

observed: slope and elevation (Copernicus GLO-30 DEM)
climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)
expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)
relative erosion index (RUSLE-type structure)
FAO suitability class boundaries on relative yield (S1>=0.8, S2 0.6-0.8, S3 0.4-0.6 [assumed], N<0.4)
simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement
feasibility score and interval (Monte-Carlo)

limiting_factors.detail: Model 1 class 5: legal/environmental restriction. Restoration potential is not assessed; the restriction itself is the limiting factor.

annual rainfall 46.0 mm (2-years-in-3 design value 39.0 mm) vs barley season ET 676.0 mm; rain-fed cultivation covers 5.0% of crop demand; climate aridity cannot be reversed, only compensated by water supply

feasibility_meta.confidence_method: 1 - width of the 5-95 % interval of the Monte-Carlo success probability over parameter draws (NOT a calibrated probability of real-world success)
feasibility_meta.score_definition: probability, over input-uncertainty x parameter draws, that at least one evaluated scenario brings the best crop to relative yield >= 0.6 (FAO class S2 or better) under a reference water allocation of 8000 m3/ha/yr per unit (a scenario condition, not an observation)

interventions.name: Pressurised drip irrigation with fertigation
interventions.description: Replaces rainfall deficit with metered water at ~80-92 % application efficiency (assumed range), allows leaching fraction control and fertigation on sandy/low-SOC soils.
interventions.expected_effect: gross water about 0.0-0.0 m3/ha/yr (central 0.0) incl. leaching, 80-92% efficiency
source_refs: FAO56: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. <https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Reclamation leaching and sustained leaching fraction
interventions.description: Apply water in excess of crop ET so that salts move below the root zone: initial reclamation depth r (m water per m soil, C/C0 = exp(-k r)) then a maintenance leaching fraction LR = ECw/(5 ECe - ECw). Needs drainage and a leachate disposal route.
interventions.expected_effect: reduce ECe 5.0 -> 0.0 dS/m (simulated); reclamation leaching depth 0.0 m water per m soil = 0.0 m3/ha one-off (C/C0 = exp(-k r), k 1.6-2.3, FAO IDP29 80-90% removal at r=1)
source_refs: FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Gypsum (or other soluble-Ca) amendment with leaching
interventions.description: Replaces exchangeable Na by Ca (0.86 g gypsum per kg soil per cmol(c)/kg of Na replaced, i.e. 1.92 t/ha pure gypsum per cmol(c)/kg for 0.15 m at 1.49 g/cm3), then leach the displaced Na.  Effectiveness fraction 0.5-0.9 assumed.
interventions.expected_effect: not required (ESP 9.2 % <= 5 % target)
source_refs: FAO_SB39: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39. <https://www.fao.org/4/x5871e/x5871e00.htm> [verified: full_text]
FAO_IDP29: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. <https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e00.htm> [verified: full_text]

interventions.name: Organic amendment / mulch (compost, manure, crop residue)
interventions.description: Raises topsoil SOC, structure and water holding; qualitative support from a rangeland meta-analysis (arid/semiarid/Mediterranean): soil carbon and water-holding capacity increase, runoff decreases; quantitative gain in this model (+0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr) is an ASSUMED range.  Low-N amendments preferred.
interventions.expected_effect: +0.05-0.40 % SOC over ~5 yr (assumed range) from 1.49 %; improves water holding and infiltration
source_refs: GRAVUER_2019: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14535> [verified: abstract]
